text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text:
Do it: Auto-apply all safe changes immediately, then log the rest for review.

This cuts cycle time by removing human bottlenecks for low-risk edits while keeping risk bounded. The trade-off is accepting a small chance of bad auto-apply—mitigated by only acting on changes we can prove safe.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t bad changes slipping through—it’s that "safe" is subjective. A better alternative: auto-apply only changes flagged by PR-Agent’s deterministic rules (e.g., formatting, docstring fixes), then log the rest. Settle it by running a 2-week pilot with strict rollback criteria and measuring error rates.

name: Overhaul
text: Run PR-Agent’s deterministic rules in a pre-commit hook instead of a post-push check, cutting latency from minutes to seconds and eliminating the need for a staging branch. This shifts risk control earlier in the flow, where fixes are cheaper and revert paths are simpler.

The trade-off is accepting a stricter gate—only rules PR-Agent flags get auto-applied, so we lose some flexibility for high-context tweaks. That’s a win: we trade occasional manual overrides for faster, safer, and more consistent improvements.
